items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And I recently wrote another one to Sir Alec Guinness.

ctx.x: No, no. No, no. I sold them a bill of goods. And I was a so-called writer so I was on the Chicago Herald Trib too, and so I said to them, “You might as well let me do the social column, because I know all these guys like Squirrel Ashcraft and all these prominent people. And that’s how I got Lawrence — Benny Goodman in the trio, because, you’ve heard about Benny, what a funny guy he was. And I was a friend of Freddy Goodman’s, who was a trumpet player manque. You know he was a wonderful musician and he didn’t

really have a lip which was very unfortunate. He had all the talent and he knew everything, but he couldn’t really cut it as a trumpet player. But anyway, we were great friends, and I said to him well Benny’s coming. And I said to Stanley the other day I wrote one fan letter in my life, and that was to Benny. And I recently wrote another one to Sir Alec Guinness. Did you read My Name Escapes Me?
